title: Hook map and compatibility report (<game>/kiln/state/hooks.json), format 1
description: Written atomically by kiln-core (kiln.hooks v2) at the end of boot, at the first world, and when links change (at most once per second; a few seconds after boot once more). `kiln.hooks.map_json` returns the same text with phase `query`. `targets` and `foreign` are the hook registry's view (WP-E); `overlaps` and `rules` are the closed-DLL report (WP-G1): where another module's hook and a Kiln-hosted hook meet, and which compat rules fired. Offsets, RVAs and addresses are hex strings (`0x...`). Readers ignore unknown keys. `pid` (added by the closed-DLL report) names the writing process; a file whose pid is not a live process is the last session's, which is what the launcher reads.

pid.description: The writing process. Absent in a core without the closed-DLL report.

phase.description: What wrote the file last. `query` only comes from map_json.

worldChecked.description: The first-world check of other modules' hooks over Kiln's has run.

linkSlots.description: Link slots taken since the game started (a revoked link keeps its slot; re-installing the same handler on the same target takes it again) and how many there are.

targets.description: Every game function Kiln hooks, one entry per physical detour.

foreign.description: Every sigdb symbol whose live code differed from the exe file's before Kiln hooked anything (someone else patched it), Kiln-hooked or not.

overlaps.description: Closed-DLL report. Absent in a core without it (dev.20).

rules.description: The compat rules that fired this session. Absent in a core without it.

ruleFiles.description: The rule files that exist (shipped defaults, then the player's); a missing file is not listed.

module.description: File name of the module the jump goes into; empty when it goes to memory outside any module (a relay stub).

address.description: The destination itself in this session (absent when no jump could be followed).

inPlace.description: Bytes were changed in place, no jump was found.

own.description: The module is one of Kiln's (`kiln-*.dll`): not an overlap.

owner.description: The registry's owner name: `service:kiln-chat.dll`, `plugin:kiln-emf.dll`, `emf:<mod id>`, `native:<id>`, a managed mod id...

symbol.description: The sigdb name of the address, null when it has none.

label.description: The symbol, else the first link's label, else `rva 0x...`.

links.description: In chain order: the first one runs first.

foreignBefore.description: Another module's jump was on the function when Kiln hooked it: Kiln's detour sits in front, the call goes on into it.

foreignOver.description: Another module hooked over Kiln's detour (found at the boot-end or first-world check). Kiln's detour stays armed behind their jump.

module.description: The other side's DLL file name. For `refused`: the only module that patched game code (probably the culprit), or null when Kiln cannot tell, and `suspects` then lists the modules that patched game code.

symbol.description: The sigdb symbol of the contested function. null for a `refused` hook that has no sigdb symbol (see `hook`).

kind.description: foreign-before: another module's hook was on the function before a Kiln-hosted link (Kiln chained over it). foreign-over: another module hooked over Kiln's detour. refused: a hosted engine could not hook the function and said so (ShroudForge's engine hooks).

owners.description: The Kiln-hosted side: who has links on the function (refused: who was refused). Names are short: the registry's `service:` / `plugin:` prefix, a leading `kiln-` and `.dll` are dropped (`shroudforge`, `chat`); engine mod owners keep their prefix (`emf:coolmod`).

hook.description: refused: the engine's own name for the hook (`game-thread`, `entity-manager`).

suspects.description: refused with an unknown `foreign.module`: the distinct modules in `foreign` (sigdb) that patched game code.

fix.description: late: the other module is a chain entry that loads early: load it late (chain.ini [late], the launcher's `Load after Kiln and ShroudForge`). rule: the other module is not a chain entry, or another loader starts it (a dinput8-chain.ini DLL while EMF's loader is chained, a DLL named in [late] that was running before the late phase, EMF's own loader, which is never deferred): add a compat rule or switch one side off. none: nothing to fix (it already loads late, or it is harmless).

path.description: The proxy's canonical path of the DLL (Windows form).

late.description: The DLL loads late (named in [late] and loaded by the core after the plugins). false for a DLL named in [late] that another loader started first.

lateIgnored.description: dev.21: named in [late], but another loader had started the DLL first, so [late] moved nothing.

chainEntry.description: The chain entry whose file name is `foreign.module`, when there is one.

message.description: The sentence kiln.log carries (both sides, and the fix).

applied.description: warn: true (it was logged). late: the subject is already a chain.ini [late] entry in this session (false for EMF's own loader, which is never deferred, and for a DLL another loader started first). disable: the subject did not load (a hosted mod the core switched off before its DLL ran, or a chain entry that is off); false for a dllmain native mod whose DLL the proxy loaded before kiln-core started. false: nothing was changed this session; `note` says what to do (`apply it in the launcher`, activate the profile again).

source.description: Which file the rule came from.

note.description: Why `applied` is false, or what was done.

rules.description: Rules read from the file that validated.

error.description: Why the file (or some of its rules) was not used; null when all fine.
